issues.failure_explanation: The formula yields a nonpositive step if the estimated sampling error is at least the squared estimated gradient norm. It also divides by zero when consecutive nonzero stochastic gradient estimates coincide, since then L̂=0. Neither event is excluded by the stated assumptions or by an enforced check. Coincident noisy estimates can occur even when the true gradients differ and the MSE is small.

issues.failure_explanation: The monitored error is constructed for the gradient ratio, not for the objective value. Objective estimation depends on θ^-1 log E[Y], whereas the gradient monitor combines X error and Y error weighted by Ĉ, which can be zero or arbitrarily small. No bound identifies its square root with objective uncertainty or with optimization error. Thus the bars do not support the stated objective-uncertainty interpretation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct Y-only bias and sampling error estimates and propagate them through the logarithm, labeling the bars as objective-estimation uncertainty at the current control. With a denominator stabilized at one, the logarithm gives the local bound objective RMSE≤Y-estimation RMSE/θ.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical uncertainty bars and the conclusions drawn specifically from their shrinking size are not justified as objective-value error estimates.
issues.title: Gradient-estimation MSE is used as objective-value uncertainty
issues.why_classification: The required scalar statistics are already computed, and a routine error-propagation correction can replace the bars without changing the optimization method or its rates.
